title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
By far the best dinner cruise I have done and a MUST do for any SOLO travellers!! For most solo travellers eating out isn’t always the best experience as most places don’t know what to do with you however this is not the case with the Charles Darwin buffet sunset harbour cruise!
Tonight I had the pleasure of sitting at my own table at the very front of the ship with 3 other solos next to me, it was great company while still making it about your individual experience and not turning it into a group booking - not to mention we clearly had the best seats on board!🤩
The food was great and all the staff were amazing! I do have to make a special mention to one of the crew tho - Lidia - what an absolute gem! Not only was she attentive to what anyone needed but she made the entire experience feel very personal! If she wasn’t working she would have made a great addition to the solo front row! 🤩🤩

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Very happy. We sat up top and the view was beautiful. Nice music and generous platters with local produce. I had the gourmet and my daughter had the garden platter. If you love meat go for the gourmet one. The weather was calm and warm. It was lovely watching as the sun set and Darwin City lights began to twinkle. This is my third time (in a span of 25 years). It's a must for me when I visit NT.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Lidia was amazing! She went above and beyond to make our night memorable. She’s very personable and charming. Thank you for a wonderful evening 🤗

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
The sunset views on the cruise were absolutely beautiful and the boat ride was calm and relaxing. Staff were friendly and the overall vibe was really nice.
I really enjoyed the food but if I had to comment one thing it would be adding more variety – especially hot meal options would really enhance the overall experience and make it feel more like a premium sunset dinner cruise.
Overall my experience was great and I would recommend to family and friends.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Amazing cruise! Would highly recommend to all my friends and family. Gabby in the office was extremely helpful

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
Part of a tour package, we did the sunset dinner cruise on a Tuesday night.

Boat left Dock 3 & check-in was very quick, then shown to a window table on lower level.

Full bar service - apparently there was table service but easier to go bar. Quality of wines quite good. Lots of can/bottles to select from

Food was buffet style - prawns, kangaroo, barra, salads, veges - quite good  barra was excellent.  Good selection of dessert & some fruit.

Scenery was nice, pre & post sunset. Didn't get much commentary regarding where we were. Disembarking was quick.

Stokes wharf very convenient for transport & lots of restaurants/bars to entertain post & pre cruise

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Interstate visitors, booked the sunset cruise gaze & graze option. Arrived early enough & followed instructions given to us to head to wharf 3, lots of people waiting with some having a dinner booking & others doing same as us. Boat has 3 levels -dining on 1st & 2nd level, G&G on the sun deck. Boarding was a bit chaotic with inpatient people & the walk down the jetty is very steep but has handrails & slip resistant tread, they managed to get everyone on board. Staff were all friendly & service was hectic for them in that first 30 mins or so with everyone wanting drinks given it was still hot in the afternoon. 6pm departure & around 7pm we had our individual gourmet platters, there was so much food on them, we could not get through it all. We sailed at a good pace & was able to enjoy all the sights along the way & staff were attentive to any needs.  Bar tabs finalised at your table & docked back around 8pm. Would highly recommend this sunset cruise to anyone looking for a great night in the water & wants to see the amazing sunsets the NT has to offer. We were staying at Adina apartments & we walked down to pier before & after cruise (10mins). Thanks to all the staff for making it a great cruise.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Really great experience cruising the harbour watching the sun set. We did the grazing option and it was really good. If you choose that, you get allocated a table on the top open deck, which was excellent. Peopleove around to get a sunset pic which is fine, although the wannabe influencers can be a tad annoying.  Definitely worth while experience.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: To put it simply, the Charles Darwin Sunset Dinner Cruise felt like a floating RSL. If that excites you then go for it, you'll probably have a great time. If that doesn't excite you, then there's plenty of other places to try in town with a modern vibe and better quality food. Food was bland and wasn't any better than your run-of-the-mill low cost buffet. Boarding was inefficient; everyone was crowded around one person looking up booking details one by one on a tablet before allowing them to board. For a moment I thought we'd miss the sunset. It was explained clearly at the beginning that first helpings of food are staggered by the staff for crowd and food management, however multiple diners disregarded this and either helped themselves when it wasn't their turn and/or helped themselves to seconds before other diners who were patiently waiting had even been invited to have their firsts, and a staff member did nothing even after being notified. There is plenty of food so you won't miss out but it was frustrating to observe and took quite a while until we had food on our plates. I wouldn't do this again personally, but there is a certain type of person who would probably find it worthwhile.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Did the sunset buffet dinner cruise, lovely boat with wonderful staff. There could have been more hot dishes but we got full. Dessert was pretty good too. Apart from the sunset the boat itself does not venture far out.  They don't ask you when you are booking but there are a number of tables on the outdoor deck, see if you can ask for one.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Really enjoyed our cruise. We purchased the buffet dinner package and the food was amazing. I struggled a little with the heat but the staff gave out little fans which helped. Enjoyed our views and had a wonderful sunset experience.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Darwin harbour sunset dinner cruise travelled late March 2025 would highly recommend this experience. From the initial greeting by the customer care consultant to my on board welcome and service. Excellent atmosphere great dining and beverage options with buffet dinner. The team have attention to detail even catering for food allergies, gluten free, lactose free and other digestive intolerances. Duration approximately 2 hours sit back in spotlessly clean environment enjoy dinner whilst taking in the views from the Charles Darwin. Thank you for a memorable positive experience

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: I’ve been taking this cruise every year for the past four years, and I can confidently say that this year was by far the best experience! The crew was incredibly attentive, the food was exceptional, and the recent renovations to the buffet and bar were fantastic. I even had the chance to enjoy a delicious frozen cocktail! I’m already looking forward to coming back next year!

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Did the buffet dinner cruise on 13 December. Staff were friendly and helpful. Sunset views were nice. Good variety of food. Commentary was advertised, however none provided. So as we cruised past all the sights, the lack of explanation as to what we were passing and its historical significance was severely lacking. As a result, 90 minutes in to a 2.5 hour cruise, we were more than ready to depart.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: We did this cruise as an excursion (a daytime cruise) booked through our cruise ship operator.   On the plus side, the staff were friendly and helpful. the 2 1/4 hour cruise was right on time, windows were clean, and there was a very nice spread of coffee, tea, and cookies and small cakes included.   Rest rooms clean (but 9 steps down; this was communicated before booking).   Unfortunately, there really wasn't much of interest to see on the cruise.   There was commentary for the first 45 minutes or so almost exclusively about WWII's effects on Darwin.   Several buildings were pointed out, and that was it.   The harbor just doesn't have enough sights (or they weren't mentioned) to occupy 2 1/4 hours.   The boat headed back and there was nothing new to see for over an hour.   Not recommended.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: Air-conditioning didn't last. Food nice but only average for the price. Staff great.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: We (party of 4) booked the Sunset Gaze & Graze cruise. This certainly did not live up to any expectations. Boarding was slow & disorganissed (why not just collect a 'boarding pass', instead of using a tablet to locate & check passengers off). The recorded commentary on the cruise was limited and at times incorrect (the Cyclone Tracy display at the Museum & Art Gallery is currently closed) and the food was the biggest disappointment. What should have been 4 platters morphed into 2 and didnt include items that were on the menu (no melon in the prosciutto, bread was a couple of dried bread sticks). On the top deck there is no direct access to the bar -have to wait for one of the staff to remember you are there!!

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises

Well worth it - if you feel the cold take a warm top just in case the wind gets up when the sun goes down. That's a tip not a complaint.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: We did the ‘Gaze and graze’ option and for what we paid, it was very disappointing. For $121 each we got a below average platter that was full of very cheap tasting/looking food. It felt like they were going for quantity over quality and it just made the food really unenjoyable when we knew how much we had paid. We then got a tiny tub of icecream to finish that my lactose friend wasn’t able to even eat and they had no other options. The whole experience was so disappointing, maybe the other experiences offered would be better, but I would not recommend the ‘Gaze and Graze’ option to anyone.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
Harbour dinner cruise on the Charles Darwin was faultless. We booked the buffet dinner which was inside the boat and there was a wide range of food with seafood, hot food and salads. All the food was exceptional. I advised them when booking that my wife was lactose intolerant and as soon as we boarded the vessel the staff were already prepared to ensure that she would have oil with the bread and not butter and came across and told her which foods had got dairy products in. There were also hot and cold desserts. Good range of drinks to purchase. The service was very attentive. We cruised into the harbour area. Saw the sunset and could go out on the deck, outside. This was undoubtably one of the highlights of our trip to Darwin and I have no hesitation in recommending it.
We used the hop on hop off bus to get to the wharf for 5.30 and we used the shuttle bus back at about 8.30 to get to the lift and walkway but it is walkable in about 30 minutes from the CBD.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
I recently went on the Darwin Harbour Dinner Cruise and was extremely disappointed. Despite the high price, the selection of food was abysmal. Not only were there only three hot dishes available, but they were also horrid. To make matters worse, the rest of the food, comprising 90% of the offerings, was served cold. We considered ourselves lucky because we had a light snack before the 'all you can eat cruise,' as when we went back for seconds, all of the hot dishes were gone. We ended up eating garden weeds and overly salty pork cubes for the rest of the night.

Adding to the frustration was the fact that the boat was massively packed with over 100 people, all crammed into the tiny main cabin. People didn't even wait until everyone had gotten the chance to go up and grab some food, leading to chaos and a rushed, unpleasant experience. To top it off, the man in charge seemingly picked tables at random, causing additional frustration for my young son. Overall, it was a complete waste of money and a terrible dining experience. I would strongly advise against anyone considering this cruise.

Went on the cruise on the 19th of April

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text:
I recently had the pleasure of taking a cruise with Darwin Harbour Cruises, and it was an experience I won't soon forget. From start to finish, everything about the experience was top-notch.

First and foremost, the seafood platter was absolutely amazing. It was clearly made with the freshest ingredients, and every item was cooked to perfection. The variety of seafood on offer was impressive, and it was all so delicious that I couldn't pick a favorite.

The service provided by the staff was also exceptional. They were friendly, attentive, and always willing to go the extra mile to make sure we were comfortable and enjoying ourselves. It was clear that they take pride in their work and genuinely care about their customers' experience.

The cruise itself was a delight as well. The boat was comfortable and well-maintained, and the views of Darwin Harbour were simply breathtaking. The knowledgeable guides provided interesting commentary throughout the cruise, giving us a deeper understanding of the area's history and wildlife.

Overall, I highly recommend Darwin Harbour Cruises to anyone visiting Darwin. Whether you're a seafood lover, a nature enthusiast, or just looking for a unique and enjoyable way to experience the beauty of Darwin Harbour, this cruise is sure to deliver. The combination of great seafood, excellent service, and stunning views make it an experience not to be missed.

title: Darwin Harbour Cruises
text: The concept of this cruise is "Enticing", however, our expectations were far from met.  Admittedly our tour was booked via Imagine Tours, not by ourselves, so we were unaware of options for inside outside seating & what that meant regarding food choices.  On arrival you all just stand on the dock, the gate opens, you file on, nothing orderly about it.  Then when you enter, you are advised that you will be seated inside, taken to the table.  Ours was by windows, with stack of outdoor chairs & a timber wooden partition, plus dirty windows (all around).  After asking the stack of chairs was halved.  We were unaware of steps down to toilets, my sister had mobility issues-but managed. The commentary was just a drone of annoyance & some relaxing background music would have been appreciated.  The commentator was like a parrot repeating what he had said a thousand times.  No ebb or flow & hard to hear.  We all just checked out & struggled to talk over him.  The staff did not keep the buffet plates stocked swiftly enough.  The commentator picked & chose which table went when.  The food was say 7/10.  One of the bowls on our table had clearly not been cleaned properly.  Bar service seemed reasonable after the initial rush.  The asian staff member stood out positively.  The table cloths were clean, the tables beneath chipboard with lifting laminex.  Large cracks in toilet floor.  However, the concept & possibilities to have a wonderful evening were there but lost in amongst the other.  I think it would be time enough for the commentator to drone on, after the sunset.  It was like lets get through all the good stuff in the first 1/2 hour.  After the sunsets - it is just dark - apart from the beautiful Ferris Wheel lights.  Orderly loading, like front deck/1st level etc. could help.  By the time we got back to dock, we all just wanted off.  If we had been seated in a half decent place, with windows we could see through, be welcomed (that bit was OK), then chill with the sunset and wine, I reckon a lot of the rest would not have even been a noticed.
